name: Acquired Dermis Elastic Tissue Disorder with Increased Elastic Tissue
aliases: Acquired Dermal Elastosis with Increased Elastic Fibers
Acquired Elastic Tissue Hyperplasia of the Dermis

criteria.description: Histopathological demonstration of increased and fragmented elastic fibers in the dermis
Presence of acquired skin changes characterized by papules, plaques, or indurated areas with altered skin texture
Exclusion of hereditary elastin disorders and other acquired elastin abnormalities by clinical and laboratory evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus clinical presentation and exclusion of other elastin disorders
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on skin biopsy and histological analysis due to lack of standardized clinical criteria.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Increased elastic fiber density in dermis confirmed by biopsy
searchTerms: more elastic fibers in skin biopsy
thicker elastic fiber layer in skin

pathognomonic.symptomName: Acquired papular or plaque-like skin lesions with altered elasticity
searchTerms: raised skin bumps or plaques with altered stretch
acquired papules or plaques with elasticity changes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized skin induration with increased dermal thickness
searchTerms: localized thickening and hardening of skin
skin feels less soft and pliable

common.symptomName: Slow progression of skin thickening over months to years

searchTerms: visible small blood vessels in skin
tiny red veins showing on skin

occasional.symptomName: Secondary skin fissuring due to decreased elasticity
searchTerms: skin cracks due to loss of elasticity

occasional.symptomName: Occasional mild pain or tenderness at lesion sites
searchTerms: occasional mild pain at skin lesions

rare.symptomName: Associated mild systemic symptoms such as low-grade fever
searchTerms: mild systemic signs like slight fever

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; absence of systemic inflammation markers
imaging: High-frequency ultrasound may show increased dermal thickness
MRI rarely used but can demonstrate dermal changes
genetic: No known genetic mutations associated; considered an acquired disorder
other: Skin biopsy with special elastic fiber stains (e.g., Verhoeff-Van Gieson) demonstrating increased elastic tissue

distinguishingFeatures: Decreased elastic fibers rather than increased
Characteristic facial features and systemic manifestations
Calcification and fragmentation of elastic fibers
Characteristic yellowish papules in flexural areas
Systemic involvement including cardiovascular and ophthalmological
Histology shows basophilic degeneration of elastic fibers

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin induration suggesting systemic sclerosis
Presence of systemic symptoms such as weight loss or fever
Ulceration or necrosis of skin lesions
references: Orphanet: Acquired Dermis Elastic Tissue Disorder with Increased Elastic Tissue, ORPHA:228224
Dermatology: 4th Edition, Bolognia et al., Chapter on Elastic Tissue Disorders
Journal of Cutaneous Pathology, 2022; Histopathological features of acquired elastic tissue disorders
